history.body: Hi, saw the Pearl ad. My partner and I are renting now and just checking whether buying around here could make sense. What should we know?

The home is 900 sq ft, with 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony. For the two of you, that could mean having room for a home office or guests as well as your shared living space. Whether buying makes sense compared with renting depends on the actual monthly cost and how long you expect to stay. What matters most in your decision: keeping the monthly commitment comfortable, or having extra room for the future?
Keeping the monthly commitment comfortable is probably the main thing. One of us does freelance work, so income can vary a bit, and we don’t want a mortgage to squeeze everything else.

That’s a sensible concern, especially with freelance income varying. One known recurring cost is maintenance: at RM0.18 per sq ft inclusive of sinking fund, the 900 sq ft home works out to about RM162 a month. That’s separate from the mortgage and other costs, so I wouldn’t want to guess at the full commitment without current unit pricing and a lender assessment. What monthly home payment would still feel comfortable in a slower freelance month?
I haven’t worked out a comfortable figure yet. We’d need to look at the likely purchase price and monthly payment together before I could say. Is there a current starting price for the units?

The lowest listed base-price reference I have is RM328,000. A package snapshot dated 14 Aug 2026 shows an indicative RM301,760 after an 8% rebate for a qualifying podium-blocked category. I can’t confirm that package is still current, and that figure isn’t an all-in unit price—parking and other applicable items can affect the final total. The monthly payment would also depend on the confirmed price, your down payment, loan terms and lender assessment, so I wouldn’t want to guess, especially with variable freelance income.
Thanks, that gives us a reference point. We’d still need the current price and an idea of the loan payment before knowing whether it works for us, especially with the variable income.

That’s the right comparison to make. The RM301,760 figure was only an indicative calculation from a dated package snapshot, not a confirmed current price. I’ll ask the team to confirm the current pricing and package. A realistic monthly repayment would also depend on the confirmed price, your deposit and loan terms, plus the lender’s assessment—so with freelance income, it’s worth checking that it still leaves room in a slower month rather than relying on a guess.
Okay, please share the confirmed pricing when you have it. Then we can compare the likely monthly commitment with our current rent.

Of course — I’ll share the current pricing once the team confirms it. Then we can use the confirmed price to work through a realistic repayment comparison with your rent; the payment will still depend on your deposit, loan terms and lender assessment.
